problem: Learning image-goal navigation from RGB only normally needs extrinsic rewards, position info or human trajectories. Prior intrinsic-reward exploration (Episodic Curiosity) fails via trivial reward maxima and has no memory-conditioned policy, and SPTM relies on expert exploration and is restricted to graph paths.
motivation: In a realistic setting the agent cannot access position, depth or external reward, and cannot be teleported, so supervision must come from the agent's own experience. The authors observe that a reachability network trained on random walks can serve as representation, novelty detector, and goal-reached detector, enabling a fully self-supervised pipeline.
key_idea: A three-stage self-supervised pipeline: learn a reachability-based visual representation, learn a memory-conditioned (Transformer over a Scene Memory Buffer) exploration policy with discrete curiosity reward, then self-generate goals from the buffer and train a navigation policy with sparse plus graph-shaped dense intrinsic rewards.
insight: The discrete curiosity reward is critical: the ablation shows continuous EC reward is exploited (agent stuck in a spot with reward just below tau) and yields poor coverage, while the discrete reward explores well. The memory-conditioned navigation policy even beats a feedforward policy trained with GT-position rewards, and the dense graph reward helps mostly for far-away goals (gap widens with distance).
method: Reachability network R (stage 1): siamese ResNet18 g plus MLP f trained by logistic regression to predict whether two random-walk frames are within k=5 steps; 800k pairs per scene.
Scene Memory Buffer: stores features g(x_t) only when the novelty score s = max_m f(g(x_t), m) < tau, so memory holds distant observations; reset each episode.

Exploration policy: small CNN then a Transformer layer (attention over SMB with temporal position embeddings) giving policy and value heads, trained with PPO on a discrete curiosity reward alpha*1[s<tau].
Graph on SMB: edges added between consecutive nearest memory elements p_{t-1}, p_t along the agent path, yielding a directed graph.
Navigation policy: concatenated CNN features of current and goal images, Transformer attention over SMB, PPO; goals are random SMB elements after a 1000-step exploration phase.
Intrinsic navigation reward: sparse beta*1[R(x_t,x*)>tau] plus dense reward of progress in shortest-path length on graph G_t to the goal.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 reachability network + 3-layer CNN + 1-layer 2-head Transformer policy (PPO), trained from scratch per scene
setting.training_data: Self-collected in-simulator experience per scene: 20 random trajectories of 20k steps (800k pairs) for R; PPO with 16 episodes of 1000 steps; no external data; separate parameters per scene, trained and tested in the same 8 scenes
setting.observation: monocular RGB 160x120 only (no depth, GPS, or compass); goal given as RGB image
setting.privileged: none at test (agent spawned at fixed entrance; GT location used only for evaluation and for the Supervised baseline)

numbers.eval_set_note: 8 selected Gibson scenes, 100 random goal locations each, same scenes used for training; 1000-step budget, success within 1 m
numbers.extra: Trained per scene with intrinsic rewards only; fixed start at entrance
numbers.evidence: Table 1, mean SPL of Ours-dense across 8 scenes

numbers_note: Only SPL per scene is in a table; success-rate and coverage results are given only in figures. Benchmark is a custom 8-scene Gibson setup, not the standard Habitat challenge.
results: Ours-dense reaches mean SPL 33.4 (sparse 30.1) versus 22.8 for a GT-position-supervised feedforward baseline, 19.2 for SPTM and 14.8 for random. Exploration coverage is comparable to a supervised coverage-reward topline and far better than vanilla Episodic Curiosity.
limitations: Trained and evaluated per scene on the same 8 scenes with fixed start position; no generalization to unseen environments is shown.
Small-scale evaluation, no standard benchmark, and the supervised baseline is a weak feedforward policy without memory.
Pipeline is not end-to-end, with separate stages and separate parameters per scene.
